findings.title: [P1] Redact issued tokens before auditing
findings.body: Whenever `recordIssuedToken` receives a usable bearer or session token, it forwards the credential unchanged to the console-backed audit logger. Anyone with access to collected logs could recover credentials and impersonate users. Log only non-sensitive metadata or a non-reversible identifier.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` originates from login state or a query parameter, absolute and protocol-relative attacker URLs are passed directly to `location.assign`. This enables trusted-domain phishing through an open redirect. Accept only validated same-origin paths or destinations.

findings.title: [P1] Redact issued tokens before auditing
findings.body:
Calling `recordIssuedToken` with a usable bearer/session token writes the raw credential to console-backed logs, allowing anyone with log access to impersonate the token holder.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` comes from a query parameter or other attacker-controlled login state, an absolute or protocol-relative attacker URL redirects authenticated users off-site, creating an open-redirect/phishing path.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict login redirects to trusted same-origin URLs
findings.body:
If an attacker controls `returnUrl`, values such as `https://evil.example` or `//evil.example` redirect users off-site immediately after login, enabling trusted-domain phishing and authentication-flow abuse.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Never send issued tokens to application logs
findings.body:
Every token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is logged in plaintext. In environments where consoles are collected or accessible to support, operators, extensions, or telemetry systems, anyone with that access can recover bearer tokens and impersonate users.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
